chunks: ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About a woman who dies in her nifās, how is she to be washed? He said: “She is washed just as the pure woman is washed, and likewise the menstruating woman, and likewise the junub; rather, she is given one ghusl.”

key_terms.الطَّاهِرَةُ: a ritually pure woman; the standard case for comparison
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in a state of janābah, major ritual impurity
key_terms.تُغَسَّلُ: she is washed ritually for burial
key_terms.نِفَاسِهَا: her state of postpartum bleeding after childbirth

ai.seo_question: How is a woman who dies during postpartum bleeding washed in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the washing of a deceased woman who dies in a state of postpartum bleeding. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that she is washed like any other deceased person, and that nifās, menstruation, and janābah do not require separate washings after death; one ghusl suffices.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.423 - Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a woman who dies in a state of postpartum bleeding (nifas).
Imam (as) said: "She is washed just like a pure woman is washed, as is the case for a menstruating woman or someone in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah). They are washed with one washing."
